headline: Man returns a painting worth thousands

sources.title: Good News Network: A Streetside Painting Salvaged for its Frame Returned After Honest Man Realized its Enormous Value
Euronews: Unemployed man takes lost Sorolla painting from Seville to Murcia
Antique Trader: Street Discovery Solves Sorolla Painting Mystery

chunks.text: In Spain, a 57-year-old man named Andrés Hurtado {{picked up}} a small painting that was leaning against a garden wall in Seville. Hurtado, a former supermarket worker from Murcia, thought someone had {{thrown it away}}. He was not really interested in the picture itself. He only wanted the beautiful golden [[frame]], so he took the painting home with him.

chunks.text: Back home in Murcia, Hurtado looked more closely at the picture. He used an AI tool and slowly {{found out}} the surprising truth. The [[artwork]] {{turned out}} to be an [[original]] work by Joaquín Sorolla, a famous 19th-century Spanish painter. An [[auction house]] in Madrid confirmed that the [[masterpiece]] was real. Experts said the painting was worth about 150,000 euros.

verbs.wrong: To begin to believe something new
verbs.correct: To learn a fact or piece of information

verbs.wrong: To be worth more than expected
verbs.correct: To be shown to be true in the end

chunks.text: Hurtado soon learned how the painting had been lost. A family in Seville had accidentally {{left it behind}} while they loaded their car for a trip to their [[beach house]]. In their hurry, they forgot it, and the police later reported the painting stolen. Many people might have wanted to {{hold on to}} such a [[valuable]] object, but Hurtado did not. He decided to {{give it back}}.

chunks.text: Hurtado contacted the police and {{handed the painting over}} so that it could go home. In the end, the artwork {{ended up}} back with its owners in Seville. Many people {{looked up to}} Hurtado for his honesty. The [[grateful]] family was so happy that they prepared a [[reward]] for him. His good choice {{paid off}}, and his story of [[honesty]] spread across Spain.

tf.s: Hurtado found out that the painting was worth about 150,000 euros.
tf.why: Hurtado found out (learned) the value after using an AI tool and getting confirmation from an auction house.

tf.s: Hurtado held on to the painting and did not return it to the family.
tf.why: Hurtado gave the painting back and handed it over to the police. Hold on to means to keep something, which is the opposite of what he did.

tf.s: The family gave the painting back by accident while they loaded their car.
tf.why: The family left the painting behind (forgot it) while loading their car. Give back means to return something to its owner, which is not what happened.

tf.s: The painting turned out to be a real work by Joaquín Sorolla.
tf.why: The painting turned out to be (was shown to be) a genuine Sorolla, and an auction house in Madrid confirmed it.

tf.s: Hurtado's honesty paid off, and the grateful family prepared a reward for him.
tf.why: His honesty paid off (brought a good result), and the grateful family prepared a reward for returning the painting.

tf.s: Hurtado threw away the painting because he was drawn to its golden frame.
tf.why: Hurtado picked up the painting (took it from the wall) because he liked the frame. Throw away means to get rid of something as trash, which is the opposite of what he did.
